findings.claim: v1 enforced the user's permissions.deny on ctx_execute, ctx_execute_file and ctx_batch_execute (hook layer and server layer). ADR-0008 'Same scope as v1' lists only 'user permissions.deny | deny' and never names the ctx tools; PRD G6 moves the policy to ~/.context-mode/policy.json with an explicit import. A Bash(rm -rf:*) deny in .claude/settings.json is then bypassed by sending the same command to ctx_execute.
findings.evidence: v1 hooks/core/routing.mjs:924-990 (ctx_execute/execute_file/batch_execute deny checks); src/server.ts:1746,2122,2127 checkDenyPolicy; src/security.ts:363-394 readBashPolicies reads .claude/settings.local.json, .claude/settings.json and every adapter global path automatically. PRD-v2.md:191 G6 'policy.json ... policy import claude is explicit'. ADR-0001:17 'deny: comes only from the user's policy file'.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY b3f93eba 2026-03-03 'feat(security): add permission enforcement for MCP sandbox tools' (from PR #34). ORIGINAL_INTENT: 'Two-layer security enforcement ... MCP execute/execute_file/batch_execute deny/ask enforcement; execute_file checks both file path (Read deny) and code (Bash deny)'. Later #451 round-3 added every adapter global path. REGRESSION_RISK: v2 re-opens the sandbox-as-deny-bypass that b3f93eba closed. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: keep auto-reading the host's own deny rules (no import step needed for them to apply); apply them inside the server to every ctx tool that runs code or reads a path, not only in the hook.
findings.fix: Add rows to the ADR-0008 scope table: ctx_execute / ctx_execute_file / ctx_batch_execute / ctx_index(path) checked against the host deny rules, in the server. State in G6 that host deny rules apply with no import; policy.json may only add rules. Add GP3 golden cases for each ctx tool.

findings.claim: 'ParseError -> allow' is fail-open. If the same parser feeds the user-deny check, any command that contains [[, ((, case, a function or <( ) skips the user's deny: `[[ 1 ]] && rm -rf ~` or `f(){ sudo x; }; f`. The ADR also never says how `bash -c '...'`, `sh -c`, `eval`, `xargs`, `env`, `command`, `$(...)` are handled; a per-argv0 decision sees argv0=bash and misses curl or a denied command inside the string.
findings.evidence: ADR-0008:24 'The decision looks at each simple command's argv0'; :51 'Result: allow and journal the code'. v1 src/security.ts:243 extractSubshellCommands and tests added in 3578242e: evaluateCommandDenyOnly("git status $(sudo rm -rf / | cat)") must deny. v1 routing.mjs:678-690 CONTEXT_MODE_REQUIRE_SECURITY=1 fail-closed.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY c1933fba 2026-06-21 'fix(security): harden shell command evaluation ... (#763)' and 3578242e 2026-06-02 'fix(security): close nested shell bypasses'; fail-closed opt-in a4ab72eb 2026-05-09 (#468 follow-up). ORIGINAL_INTENT: 'Implement recursive subshell command extraction'; 'close nested shell bypasses'. REGRESSION_RISK: v2 re-opens #763 and #468. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: no regex (owner); parser must recurse into $( ), backticks, bash/sh -c, eval strings.
findings.fix: Split the rule: for routing (size) a ParseError may allow; for user deny rules a ParseError must deny with the code (fail closed, one path). Add parser recursion into $( ), backticks, and the string arg of bash/sh/zsh -c and eval. Add GP3 cases for each, plus the v1 3578242e test inputs.

findings.claim: Case B returns permissionDecision 'allow' + updatedInput for subagent Bash. In Claude Code, 'allow' from a PreToolUse hook skips the permission prompt, so every subagent Bash command that the user would be asked about (or that a permissions ask rule covers) runs with no prompt. The hook auto-approves arbitrary commands. Also the rewritten text is `node run.mjs <base64>`, so the host's own Bash(...) rules and other hooks no longer see the real command.
findings.evidence: ADR-0016:27 'PreToolUse returns allow + updatedInput. The command becomes node <bundle>/run.mjs <base64 of the original>'. v1 hooks/core/formatters.mjs:22-28 (allow+updatedInput semantics). Claude Code hook docs say allow bypasses the permission system [U: not fetched in this review].
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY 4bc292fc 2026-05-31 'fix(hooks): claude-code Bash modify -> deny (CC ignores updatedInput.command)'. ORIGINAL_INTENT: 'CC v2.1.x Bash tool ignores updatedInput.command substitution under permissionDecision: allow ... Only deny is honored'. REGRESSION_RISK: v2 relies on the exact path v1 proved dead (LV1 open) and, if it works, it is a permission bypass. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: never widen what the user's permission mode allows.
findings.fix: Before rewrite, evaluate the original command against host deny/ask rules and the session permission mode; deny -> deny; ask or not pre-approved -> emit 'ask' with updatedInput (or no decision), never 'allow'. LV1/LV9 must assert a prompt still appears for a non-allowlisted command.

findings.claim: The follow-up line `more: node <bundle>/search.mjs <source-id> "<terms>"` puts model-derived text (the description/intent) inside double quotes in a shell line that the subagent is told to run. Terms with `$(...)`, backticks or `"` give command injection. Also base64 of the original in argv: macOS ARG_MAX is 1,048,576 B and base64 adds 33%, so big heredoc commands fail with E2BIG; argv is also visible to other local users in ps.
findings.evidence: ADR-0016:27 quoted line. `getconf ARG_MAX` -> 1048576 on the owner's Mac.
findings.archaeology: New in v2; no v1 equivalent.
findings.fix: Encode terms the same way as the command (base64 or single-quoted with ' escaped), or print only `search.mjs <source-id>` and read terms from stdin. Pass the original command through a temp file (0600) or stdin, not argv. Add GP3 cases with $( ) in description and a 900 KB command.

findings.claim: Change #2 allows curl when 'written to a file (-o file, -O, >)'. It drops v1's checks for stdout aliases (-o -, -o /dev/stdout, -O -), verbose/trace flags that flood stderr, and the silent flag. `curl -o /dev/stdout URL` and `curl -v -o f URL` would be allowed and flood context.
findings.evidence: v1 hooks/core/routing.mjs:744-758 stdout alias and verbose checks. ADR-0008:25, :58 golden cases list none of these.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY 2731ca25 2026-03-22 'feat: allow curl/wget with silent file-output, block stdout floods (#166)'. ORIGINAL_INTENT: 'Allow when ALL conditions met: 1. Output to file 2. NOT stdout alias (-o -, /dev/stdout) 3. Silent flag 4. No verbose/trace flags'. REGRESSION_RISK: re-breaks #166 flood guard. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: keep #166 allow cases allowed.
findings.fix: Define 'file' as a path that is not -, /dev/stdout, /dev/stderr, /dev/fd/1|2, /proc/self/fd/1; treat -v/--trace/-D - as reaching output. Add GP3 rows for each.

findings.claim: On Claude Code the PreToolUse hook is type mcp_tool and 'runs only while this session's server is connected; otherwise the tool runs'. If user deny rules are also enforced only by this hook, a server that is down, slow to start or crashed turns all user denies off. v1 ran the security stage before and independent of isMCPReady().
findings.evidence: ADR-0008:27. v1 routing.mjs:28-30 mcpRedirect checks isMCPReady() only for redirects; Stage 1 security at :707-720 runs without it.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY 74f52143 2026-05-08 'Fix/security fail open build missing (#468)' and a4ab72eb (fail-closed opt-in). ORIGINAL_INTENT: user deny patterns 'may target Read/Write paths that would otherwise leak before security loads'. REGRESSION_RISK: #468 class (silent fail-open of deny). SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: routing may be readiness-gated; user deny may not.
findings.fix: State that only routing denies are tied to server readiness. User deny rules stay with the host's own permission engine (Claude Code enforces permissions.deny itself) and with the server for ctx tools (SEC-1); doctor reports any agent where deny depends on the server.

findings.claim: G6 reads a project-level `.context-mode/policy.json`, and ADR-0008 #6 adds an allowHosts list there. A cloned repo can ship this file and widen WebFetch hosts or weaken rules for anyone who opens it. The docs do not say project policy may only tighten.
findings.evidence: PRD-v2.md:191 '~/.context-mode/policy.json + .context-mode/policy.json'; ADR-0008:29 'A user policy file with an allowHosts list'.
findings.archaeology: v1 readBashPolicies (src/security.ts:369-377) also reads project .claude/settings*.json, but the host itself gates trust of project settings. New surface in v2.
findings.fix: allowHosts and any allow rule only from the user file; project file can only add deny rules. Add a GP3 case: project policy with allowHosts is ignored and doctor reports it.

findings.claim: release.yml takes any `sha` input and publishes it to `release`. Nothing checks that the sha is on origin/v2 or that ci passed on it. Clients (Claude Code, Codex, Pi) install the branch tip, not a tag, so SHA256SUMS and the attestation are never checked on install; ctx_upgrade 'verify the bundle hash' has no stated trust source (same branch = circular). No branch protection or ruleset for `release` is stated, and no pinning of third-party actions (git-cliff).
findings.evidence: ADR-0013:31 'input sha'; :37-38 SHA256SUMS + attestation; ADR-0011:13 Codex and Pi see only new commits, not tags; ADR-0010:45 'verify the bundle hash'; TECH-SPEC.md:232. No 'ruleset' or 'protect' in any v2 doc (grep).
findings.archaeology: v1 bundle.yml has contents: write and pushes bundles to main; no release-branch precedent.
findings.fix: plan job: fail unless `git merge-base --is-ancestor $sha origin/v2` and ci is green on it. Ruleset on `release`: no force push, no delete, only the release workflow may push. Pin all actions by full sha. ctx_upgrade verifies with `gh attestation verify` or a hash fetched from the GitHub Release of the matching tag, not from the branch.

findings.claim: Owner rule: the issue template must be written fully for AI agents; an agent that reads it must follow our rules and send the maximum debug data. bug.yml is written for a human ('Run /ctx-doctor, or tell the agent'). It gives the agent no rules for the free-text fields (what happened / steps), so an agent can paste commands, paths, tokens or transcript text there; the typed redaction covers only the report block.
findings.evidence: ADR-0014:57 bug.yml row; :38-43 redaction applies to report values only.
findings.archaeology: v1 bug_report.yml required ctx-debug.sh output (4eba5aaf 2026-04-03, 6799caaf) and that caused #1141 'bug_report.yml requires pasting this into public issues'. REGRESSION_RISK: secrets move from the report to the free-text fields.
findings.fix: Rewrite bug.yml as agent instructions: call ctx_doctor and paste its block unedited; for the free-text fields, give the exact fields to fill (denied tool, alternative, ctx error codes) and forbid paths, env, tokens and transcript text. Get maximum data by adding more typed rows to the report, not free text. Add a GP11-style check on the template text.

findings.claim: `digest: <sha256>` and the test 'the digest verifies' prove only that nobody changed bytes by accident. Anyone (or the agent) can edit the report and recompute it. The doc does not say what is hashed or that it is not an authenticity check.
findings.fix: State what bytes are hashed and that the digest is a copy-check, not proof of origin. Do not use it to trust a report.
